title: OpenAI o1: Learning to Reason with Reinforcement Learning
hook: OpenAI's o1 lets a model think via a long internal chain-of-thought before answering - spending more compute at inference time visibly improves reasoning.
key_points: Trained with RL to generate an extended internal reasoning trace before producing its final answer.
More 'thinking' tokens at inference time correlates with better performance on hard reasoning tasks.
Outperformed PhD-level humans on select science benchmarks and ranked highly on math competitions.
Kicked off the 'reasoning model' era, with competitors quickly following with similar approaches.
content_html: OpenAI released o1 in September 2024, a model trained with reinforcement learning to produce an extended internal reasoning trace before delivering its final response. Rather than answering immediately, o1 "thinks out loud" in a hidden scratchpad, then returns a polished answer.
extra_html:
How it works

o1 is trained with RL to maximize correctness on problems with verifiable answers. During training, the model learns to use its reasoning trace to explore, backtrack, and self-correct. At inference time, giving the model more "thinking" budget - more tokens in that trace - consistently improves accuracy, trading compute for quality.

Why it matters

Before o1, scaling meant training bigger models; o1 showed that scaling inference-time compute is a complementary axis. This "reasoning model" framing - where thinking longer produces better answers - launched a wave of similar work, including open-source efforts like DeepSeek-R1. Read OpenAI's full technical post for benchmark details and the RL training setup.

related.hook: Sample the model many times, let each run reason its own way, then take the majority answer - diverse reasoning paths vote out individual errors.

related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.
